rules.benefit: Sections 3-37-15 and 3-37-16 identify medium-high and high-density residential districts. Compare a multifamily scheme with the applicable district’s use table.
rules.caution: Check the planning-area chapter and whether master-plan review applies before estimating unit yield.

rules.benefit: A multi-use or transit-oriented designation gives a reason to investigate housing alongside other uses.
rules.caution: Read the precise district and planning-area use tables. The label alone does not establish that a particular housing project is permitted.

rules.benefit: Section 41-259 lists multifamily dwellings as a permitted use, making an apartment proposal worth testing against the R3 standards.
rules.caution: Townhouses follow different design standards. Verify lot size, setbacks and project form under the applicable division.

rules.benefit: Section 41-247 lists two-family homes and townhouses among permitted uses. This supports screening a smaller affordable development.
rules.caution: Townhouses have separate design standards under Division 6. Larger apartment schemes require an independently supported route.

rules.benefit: A detached affordable home is consistent with the district’s single-family residential purpose.
rules.caution: For a larger apartment proposal, establish an alternative planning or state-law route before estimating capacity. Check the current §41-232 use list and any overlay.

rules.benefit: The city maps this as a suburban apartment district, so an apartment layout is worth testing against district standards.
rules.caution: Confirm the permitted use, minimum lot size and density for the specific site; the map alone supplies none of those quantities.

rules.benefit: Article XIX provides a transit zoning code with sub-zones and use tables for site-specific housing research.
rules.caution: Identify the sub-zone and overlays before assigning allowed uses, building type or approval process. SD84 alone is too broad.

rules.benefit: Table 6-A designates multifamily dwellings as a permitted use in these districts.
rules.caution: Check the special provisions in §§18.38.100 and 18.40.090 and project development standards before calculating capacity.

rules.benefit: Table 6-A identifies a route without a conditional-use permit for qualifying affordable developments on eligible sites.
rules.caution: Outside that exception, multifamily dwellings require a conditional-use permit under the local table. Verify eligibility under §18.38.023.

rules.benefit: Table 8-A identifies an affordable-development exception for multifamily housing on eligible sites.
rules.caution: The multifamily row is otherwise prohibited under the local table. Verify §18.38.023 eligibility and applicable overlays.

rules.benefit: Table 8-A marks multifamily dwellings as a permitted use, subject to its special provisions.
rules.caution: Check the General Plan designation and implementing zone under §18.08.030.150 where applicable. Motel or office conversions carry separate conditions.

rules.benefit: Table 13-32 gives an R3 base density of one dwelling per 2,178 square feet of gross land area.
rules.caution: The table also specifies minimum lot area and open space. Common-interest developments have separate standards.

rules.benefit: Table 13-32 provides a base density of one dwelling per 3,000 square feet of gross land area.
rules.caution: Check lot area, open space, and the provisions applicable to the development’s ownership form.

rules.benefit: Table 13-32 gives a base density of one dwelling per 3,630 square feet, with a specific exception for certain older lots.
rules.caution: The older-lot exception depends on creation date and lot area. Confirm both before relying on the exception.

rules.benefit: The base R-2 multifamily standards list a maximum of 21 units per acre. Qualifying projects can investigate a state density bonus.
rules.caution: The permissible footprint can shrink beside R-1 property because upper floors face additional stepbacks.

rules.benefit: The base R-3 multifamily standards list a maximum of 32 units per acre. Qualifying projects can investigate a state density bonus.
rules.caution: The base table limits height to 35 feet and three stories, with additional stepbacks beside R-1 property. Check exceptions and waivers.

LF.title: Lake Forest Municipal Code, Planning and Zoning

rules.benefit: Chapter 9.56 lists multifamily dwellings of four units or fewer among principal permitted uses.
rules.caution: Five or more units generally require a site-development permit under §9.56.030. Specified common-interest projects follow separate provisions.

rules.benefit: The R1 district provides a starting point for evaluating a detached-home layout.
rules.caution: A conventional apartment project needs a separately supported pathway. Check whether state law or another site-specific provision changes the local baseline.

rules.benefit: Section 9.73.020 allows an entirely residential project and sets a base maximum of 32 units per net acre.
rules.caution: Check net developable area, open-space requirements and any specific-plan requirement at Foothill Ranch Town Center.

rules.benefit: Section 9.73.030 allows entirely residential projects as well as mixed-use projects.
rules.caution: Check the district’s residential density and open-space standards; a scheme that also includes businesses must meet the nonresidential floor-area requirements.

rules.benefit: Chapter 9.73 expressly includes residential uses and all-residential projects in Urban Industrial 25.
rules.caution: Screen surrounding industrial uses for compatibility and check the district’s residential development standards.

pathways.title: State Density Bonus Law · Government Code §65915
pathways.benefit: Qualifying housing developments can obtain added density and, where statutory criteria are met, concessions, waivers or reduced parking.
pathways.caution: Check project size, unit mix, income levels and affordability commitments. A mapped district does not establish eligibility or the size of a bonus.

pathways.title: AB 2011 · Government Code §§65912.100–65912.140
pathways.benefit: Screen qualifying commercially zoned sites for the 100% affordable route, or eligible commercial corridors for the mixed-income route. Eligible projects receive ministerial review.
pathways.caution: Check allowed commercial uses, site and corridor criteria, affordability, labour requirements and exclusions for the chosen route.

pathways.title: SB 4 · Government Code §65913.16
pathways.benefit: Certain 100% affordable projects on land owned by religious or higher education institutions may qualify for ministerial approval.
pathways.caution: Verify qualifying ownership before 1 January 2024 and the affordability, location, wage and demolition conditions. Institutional zoning alone is insufficient.
